shortDefinition: A sampling method that selects from the smallest set of top probable tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold.
fullDefinition: Top-p, also called nucleus sampling, is an alternative to temperature for controlling output randomness. Instead of considering all possible tokens, top-p selects from only the smallest set of most probable tokens whose combined probability exceeds a threshold p. For example, with p=0.9, the model considers only the smallest group of likely tokens whose probabilities sum to 90%. This dynamic filtering prevents the model from wasting probability mass on extremely unlikely tokens while maintaining diversity. Top-p is often used together with temperature to fine-tune the quality and variety of model outputs.
examples: Using top-p=0.95 for a chatbot to allow natural variation without strange outputs
Setting top-p=0.5 for technical writing to keep responses focused
Combining low temperature with top-p=0.9 for reliable but varied outputs
